title: Nomi Prins: We’re Forecasting $6,000 Gold - By The End Of The Year
speaker: Nomi Prins (guest); host Daryl Thomas

macro_themes.view: Retail/Western confidence returning after Iran-war headline selling; ETF buying of gold and silver to continue into year-end rebalancing.
Central banks will keep accumulating physical gold and repatriating it rather than chase 5% Treasury yields.
Fewer buyers for growing US debt; Treasury buybacks and eventual Fed QE will grow.
Rate hikes cannot fix oil-driven inflation; more hikes depend on oil prices, not core inflation.
Lower oil (e.g., Iran resolution) would cut CPI/PPI and boost gold.

calls.condition: Iran resolution / lower oil would add further upside momentum.
calls.reason: Stable base at 4300-4400 after digesting Fed hike; returning ETF inflows, central-bank buying, strong miner margins, debt crisis; target $6,000 by end of 2026 or mid-January.
calls.quote: we're still predicting $6,000, um, for gold by the end of the year.

calls.reason: All-in costs 1800-2200 vs gold at 4300-4400 imply excellent profits and cash flow; upcoming quarterly reports should add momentum.
calls.quote: So we will continue to see good reports from these companies.

notes: No date stated in transcript ("October is already upon us"), so listing approx_date used. Gold price_at_call is the midpoint of the 4300-4400 range she cited. Target $6,000 by year-end (~3 months) placed in medium_term. Silver mentioned only alongside gold ETF flows; not recorded. She never recommends bonds.
